title: Man-in-the-middle attacks in under a minute
description: A man-in-the-middle attack puts a stranger between you and the website you're using. Here's how it works and how HTTPS keeps it in check.

scenes.say: A man-in-the-middle attack puts a stranger between you and a website, passing messages along while reading them.

steps: You join a fake Wi-Fi hotspot
They read or change what passes
scenes.say: It often starts with a fake Wi-Fi hotspot, named like a real café's. Your traffic flows through the attacker, who can read or change anything unprotected, while everything looks normal.

scenes.sub: encryption, plus proof of who's there
scenes.say: The defence is HTTPS. It encrypts your traffic, and certificates prove the site is genuine. So a middleman sees scrambled data, and can't easily pose as the real site.

scenes.caption: Someone in between
scenes.say: If your browser shows a warning like this, stop. It might be harmless, but it's exactly what interception can look like. Don't click through.
So check the network name, keep devices updated, and never ignore certificate warnings. Follow, and catch the next threat soon.
